title: W1 drawn-tile cap predicate is not mirrored into growth_board_cluster_has_room — a cap-locked ring burns the whole window budget and the SEED family is never reached (permanent board-wide growth stop while seed budget exists)
location: core/growth.odin:620-655 (growth_board_cluster_has_room) vs core/growth.odin:959-968 (the W1 rejection) + core/map_test.odin:584-606
evidence: growth.odin:620-625: "// growth_board_cluster_has_room — the board-aware ATTACH eligibility: a // cluster is eligible to extend only while SOME member's ring holds a tile // that can still be placed legally (the E31 node/pipe separation + the // connect span — the same predicates the draw faces, checked ahead so a // saturated estate yields to the SEED family instead of stalling the window // budget). Pure scans, zero rng (deterministic)." — its tile loop checks only: "for k in ring { c := board.candidates[k] if !growth_node_sep_ok(t, c, sep) { continue } if !growth_pipe_sep_ok(t, c, sep) { continue } if !growth_connectable(t, c, span) { continue } return true }". The fold's W1 predicate (growth.odin:966) adds a draw-time check the eligibility scan lacks: "if growth_district_live_count(board, t, map_district_assign(board, pos)) >= growth_district_cap(board, cat, map_district_assign(board, pos)) { continue }" inside "for attempt in 0..<GROWTH_MAX_ATTEMPTS". The SEED family runs only when the cluster scan finds none ("eligible > 0" gates the attach branch; bias defaults 1000, so every attempt takes it). The pin's own comment confirms the realized behavior (map_test.odin test_growth_dublin_attach_tile_district_cap): "with it every attempt rejects deterministically (the ring never changes; the bounded budget exhausts; the window skips)."
detail: has_room checks E31 predicates only; the W1 cap rejects at draw time. When every E31-clear ring tile of the sole eligible estate sits in capped districts, all 8 attempts reject each window; state never changes, so the stall is permanent while other districts still hold seed budget — the documented yield-to-SEED invariant breaks.
recommended_fix: Mirror W1 into growth_board_cluster_has_room: a ring tile counts as room only when its OWN district is under cap, so a cap-locked estate becomes ineligible and the SEED family takes the window.

title: The W1 pin passes vacuously on the zero-spawn path it itself documents — no spawn-count assertion, so the full-stall outcome is blessed silently
location: core/map_test.odin:603-610 (test_growth_dublin_attach_tile_district_cap) vs the sibling pin at core/map_test.odin:459-461
evidence: test_growth_dublin_attach_tile_district_cap body: "spawns := director_growth_run(t, cat, &board, 1000, routers[:], seeds[:], 3 * cat.balance.terminal_spawn_interval_ticks) defer delete(spawns) for p in spawns { testing.expectf(t, map_district_assign(&board, p) == 0, \"spawn %v must NOT land in B — B is at its cap (the drawn tile's district is cap-checked)\", p) }" — no len(spawns) assertion. The sibling cap pin asserts growth continues: "testing.expectf(t, len(spawns) > 0, \"growth must continue in the uncapped district\")". The comment above documents the zero-spawn outcome: "with it every attempt rejects deterministically (the ring never changes; the bounded budget exhausts; the window skips)."
detail: The assertion loop passes vacuously on an empty spawn list — the pin cannot distinguish 'W1 correctly rejected B' from 'all growth died' (ring-scan, member-pick, or eligibility regressions killing spawns entirely also pass).
recommended_fix: Assert the spawn count explicitly (len==0 today documents the stall; once has_room models the cap, seeds land in A and the no-B assertion gains teeth).
